title: IS12:: power.c (10.3)

lines.code: /* Example power.c: Calculating Power with functions

lines.explanation: This is a prototype fof the function power. It tells that power has two integer parameters and returns an integer
This loop will execute 9 times with i running from 0 to 8. For each i we will print the value of 2 power i and -3 power i

To calculate the expression power(2, i), the function power will be called. The constant 2 will be passed in and assigned to the first formal parameter (base) and the current value of i, to the second parameter (n)

To calculate the expression power(3, i), the function power will be called. The constant 3 will be passed in and assigned to the first formal parameter (base) and the current value of i, to the second parameter (n)
This line will print for each i the value of i itself and values of 2 power i and -3 power i calculated by the function power

lines.code: /* power: raise base to n-th power n >= 0 */

lines.explanation: This is the header of the function. Two integer formal parameters are defined here. The first is base and the second is n. Inside the function, base and n works as any other local variables. You can use and change their values.
These are local variables of the function power(). They are not accessible from main(). After the function call is completed, their values will be lost
The goal of this loop is to base on itself exactly n times. p serves as a working variable for that
This statement can also be written as p *= base;
The value of the expression in return operator (here it is p) is calculated and returned to the calling program. It will be the value of the funcion call expression.
